title: Galleria Diagnostics customer intake - raw notes
content:
Meeting: intro sync + technical intake with Galleria Diagnostics (radiology AI/triage)
Date: 2026-03-10 11:00 PT (30m)
Attendees: Dr. Elena Sousa (Galleria), Ryan Holt (CT Ops), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Owen Ramirez (Redwood Solutions), Kira Chen (Redwood PM)

Objective:
- Quick intake of production requirements and constraints for a Proof-of-Concept: radiology report summarization + priority triage. Determine feasibility for Private deployment (VPC) vs Hosted API.

High-level asks from Galleria:
- Near-real-time short summary (1-2 sentence triage) for incoming radiology reports: target p95 latency < 300ms for typical 600-token input.
- More detailed structured summary (bulleted findings, impression, follow-ups) for clinician UI: target p95 < 2s for longer inputs (4k-8k tokens).
- Embeddings for semantic search across historical reports (~6M documents).
- Strong data isolation (PHI) — must be HIPAA-compatible, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and on-prem option for air-gapped labs.
- Deterministic rollouts + quick fallback to a smaller model for outages.
- Cost sensitivity: conservative monthly budget for POC.

Notes / technical constraints mentioned by customer:
- Source artifacts are DICOMs + extracted report text; conversion pipeline sometimes leaves newline noise and OCR artifacts. We need robust prompt templates and sanitization.
- Average report length: 1.2k tokens; 90th percentile: ~7.5k tokens (long cross-sectional studies).
- They want to keep raw PHI in their VPC; Redwood Private control plane preferred.
- Existing infra: AWS account with VPC, EKS cluster for app components, S3 for archive, HashiCorp Vault for secrets (they prefer HSM for key wrapping).
- GPU preference: they currently have access to p4/a100 equivalents in prod; evaluating H100 for larger context experiments.
- Ops team can manage container images but not model weights. They prefer Redwood to host model artifacts in Private flow (pull from S3 or our registry).

Immediate gotchas / risk flags I logged:
- Context window: 8k+ cases will push memory usage — we may need to recommend quantized 4-bit variants or chunked prompting with KV cache.
- Latency SLOs for 300ms p95 are aggressive on shared infra; will likely require Dedicated or Private pinned capacity with small batch sizes. Must call this out in SLO doc.
- Embedding index size (~6M x 512 dims) — client expects semantic search; need to discuss whether they want Redwood to host vector DB or integrate with their Pinecone/Weaviate. Also storage/throughput costs.
- PHI rules: they want audit-level logs of token payloads for QA but cannot allow raw PHI to leave their VPC. We need to map out what our audit hooks can capture without exfiltrating sensitive text.
- OCR noise + tokenization: common prompt hallucination vector. Need canonical prompt sanitization and fail-safe flags when input confidence is low.

Suggested Redwood approach (initial POC):
- Phase 0 (prep): get account contact + compliance NDA, exchange architecture diagram, confirm Vault/HSM approach and KMS key policies.
- Phase 1 (POC): Private deployment in their AWS VPC (control plane in Redwood-hosted but no PHI leaves VPC) or fully private control plane (if legal requires). Start with a mid-sized open model (32k-window variant if available or 8k with chunking) quantized to int8/4 depending on memory.
  - Provision: 2 dedicated GPU nodes (A100/H100 depending on pricing) behind Redwood serving runtime, configure autoscale policy with burst disabled.
  - Networking: VPC peering or PrivateLink; Egress controls to prevent data exfil.
  - KMS: integrate their Vault + AWS KMS; HSM for key wrap if required.
- Phase 2 (evaluation): measure latency for representative dataset (1000 requests across distribution), run quality evals on clinician-labeled prompts (we should collect 200 labeled gold summaries).
- Phase 3 (rollout): define canary traffic split, fallback routing to smaller/cheaper variant. Define alert thresholds for latency, error rate, regression in summary quality.

Operational notes / config ideas:
- Model selection: start with a high-recall summarization variant. Provide two endpoints: triage-short (low-latency, small context, constrained tokens) and triage-full (higher-latency, structured JSON output).
- Prompt engineering: include a pre-sanitize step to remove obvious PHI markers for QA flow; preserve content for model but mask in logs.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for repeated templates (radiology templates often repetitive) to reduce token cost.
- Batching: keep batch size = 1 for triage-short to meet latency targets; allow small batches for triage-full during lower load windows.
- Quantization: evaluate Q4 and int8 — run perf tests to validate latency/quality tradeoffs.

Data / eval plan to propose to customer:
- Collect 200 clinician-verified summaries to use as an eval set. We'll run ROUGE/BLEU + human review for precision/recall of findings.
- Latency tests: run synthetic replay of 1k requests sampled from their archive across length buckets (<=1k, 1k-4k, >4k).
- Safety checks: test prompt injections / redaction checks to ensure PHI not leaking into risk logs.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Send NDA + compliance questionnaire template to Dr. Sousa (Maya) — ETA 2026-03-11.
- Create initial architecture sketch (VPC/peering options + KMS flow) and share with Ryan — (Owen) ETA 2026-03-13.
- Spin up small perf harness for 8k-window quantized model on Dedicated infra and run 100 sample latency runs (Kira) ETA 2026-03-17.
- Draft POC SOW (1-month) with pricing scenarios: Hosted trial, Dedicated reserved, Private (Redwood-managed) — (Maya/Owen) ETA 2026-03-14.
- Ask customer for 200 anonymized example reports (can be synthetic if necessary) and one-week sample traffic profile (Ryan) — requested in follow-up email.

Notes to self / internal reminders:
- Emphasize that 'no raw PHI leaves VPC' is negotiable only if they accept our Private control plane deployment; double-check legal on our side.
- Prepare fallback model mapping (model A -> model B) in case capacity constrained; include cost delta estimates.
- Check if Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profile automatically for their distribution — coordinate with Applied ML.
- Flag SRE for possible burst capacity requirements during overnight batch indexing of embeddings (6M docs could need bulk ingest).

Follow-up meeting: schedule POC kickoff week of 2026-03-22 (30–45m) pending NDA and SOW sign-off.

Random scribbles captured during call (raw, keep as-is):
- "PDFs sometimes have trailing headers repeated — strip duplicates before prompt"
- "Can we do on-prem? Lab legal says maybe w/air-gapped image repo"
- "If we can't host vectors, we might stream embeddings to their Weaviate cluster"
- "Prefer streaming triage for UI so clinician sees partial answer ASAP"

End of notes.
